storyboard.claim: Being bonded can make a person lose their sense of self.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther slumped and grieving, the bonded commander as the picture of a self being lost.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Cold open of the episode, a general relationship truth.
storyboard.addedInformation: Puts the bond's cost on Luther's body before the host explains it.
storyboard.staging: Luther slumps in sadness: the self he is losing is the subject.

storyboard.claim: Independent choices are overridden by attachment, which is terrifying.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon with Luther thinking, bound by something he cannot choose.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the loss of self into the mechanism of the bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains literally show the bound state the narrator calls overriding.
storyboard.staging: Worried thinker with chains: he is held by the attachment he did not choose.

storyboard.claim: Luther commands armies while the world burns.
storyboard.concreteVisual: War icon with Luther pointing, the commander giving orders in a burning world.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Applies the everyday fear to a commander at war.
storyboard.addedInformation: Makes the command role and the wider war visible at once.
storyboard.staging: Luther points with an angry face: he is the commander driving the war.

storyboard.claim: The magical bond subverts how grand conflicts are normally read.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host framing only; no literal icon fits a subversion of logic.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the bond matters more than the army.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the reframing the hosts are about to argue for.
storyboard.staging: Callout carries the claim; no picture is drawn for an abstract reframing.

storyboard.claim: Fantasy usually treats epic wars as a chess game of generals and supply lines.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A game icon, the literal chess-like board of the usual war model.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Starts the chess metaphor the next beats overturn.
storyboard.addedInformation: Draws the genre convention as a game board the viewer can read literally.
storyboard.staging: Game icon as the familiar model of war being set up.

storyboard.claim: The book does not flip the chess board; it burns the pieces.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Fire icon standing for the pieces set alight and thrown away.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Breaks the chess model from the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The fire is literal: the chess pieces are on fire.
storyboard.staging: Fire icon shows the literal burning of the game pieces.

storyboard.claim: The magical bond overrides free will and tactical minds.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther worried and thinking, his tactical mind under a bond he cannot argue with.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the pieces cannot be moved logically.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the bond as the force that defeats strategy.
storyboard.staging: A worried commander: the bond beats his thinking, shown on his face.

storyboard.claim: A crown's loyalty is tested not in battle but in the bond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The struck phrase carries the rejection; Luther stands worried, no battle drawn.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Sets the thesis: the test is private, not on the battlefield.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the expected battlefield reading so the viewer sees the rejection.
storyboard.staging: No battle imagery: a battle would show what the narrator rejects.

storyboard.claim: The loyalty test is an inescapable bond the crown cannot choose.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther sad and still, the bonded crown with no choice.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Narrows the test to the private bond.
storyboard.addedInformation: States that the bond was not chosen, which the viewer cannot read from a face alone.
storyboard.staging: Sad idle face carries the no-choice grief; the callout names the bond.

explainedBy: Structure: three private stakes, forced alliances, magical tethering and inescapable bloodlines, that decide the war.

storyboard.claim: The war is decided by three private stakes.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Three buckets, one per private stake.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Names what the private stakes are.
storyboard.addedInformation: Lists the three stakes the narration gives.

storyboard.claim: The situation is a total mess.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Host framing only; the callout carries the verdict.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Banter that sets up laying out the board.
storyboard.addedInformation: Gives the viewer the hosts' verdict on the board.
storyboard.staging: Callout only; no literal image of a mess.

storyboard.claim: Amarian is in absolute, unprecedented chaos.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The Realm wide across the horizon, the whole continent in view.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Begins the board overview with the continent.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the continent-scale scope the narrator describes.
storyboard.staging: Wide horizon set: the chaos is the whole continent, not a skirmish.

storyboard.claim: Omnos is an ancient god of shadows, imprisoned for millennia.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Chains icon with a shadowed silhouette: a god bound in darkness.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: First front of the war: the imprisoned god.
storyboard.addedInformation: Chains read literally as the imprisonment the narrator describes.
storyboard.staging: Silhouette with chains: the god is shown bound and in shadow.

storyboard.claim: Omnos's army has one goal: slaughter every descended person.
storyboard.concreteVisual: A shadowed abstract set; no single figure, since a crowd would read as duplicates.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the god's goal after the imprisonment.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the genocidal goal, which the viewer cannot read from a picture.
storyboard.staging: Callout carries the goal; the set stays dark and empty.

storyboard.claim: A separate conflict is boiling over in the south.
storyboard.concreteVisual: The wide horizon set for a second front across the land.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Adds the second front after the god.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places a second conflict in the south of the continent.
storyboard.staging: Wide set with the callout naming the southern conflict.

storyboard.claim: The mortals have organized a massive rebellion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: War icon for the mortal rebellion against the rulers.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The second front is the mortal rebellion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the rebellion as the mortals' organized armed uprising.
storyboard.staging: War icon with the callout: the rebellion is the war.

explainedBy: Comparison: an ancient threat from above versus a mortal rebellion from below, two forces pressing the crowns from opposite sides.

storyboard.claim: Two forces press from above and from below.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Empty frame; the callout sets the above-versus-below comparison.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Joins the two fronts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the threat from above against the rebellion below.

storyboard.claim: The crowns force an uneasy alliance to hold the realms together.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther worried in front of the wide Realm, the crown holding the alliance.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Brings the crowns into the middle of the two fronts.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the alliance is uneasy, which the worried face shows.
storyboard.staging: Worried idle face in the realm: the alliance is strained.

storyboard.claim: The crowns' minds and bodies are compromised by each other.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther sad and thinking, a compromised mind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the alliance is fragile.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the compromise both minds and bodies suffer.
storyboard.staging: Sad thinker: the compromise is the grief of a compromised mind.

storyboard.claim: The first casualty is a commander's strategic mind, not a foot soldier.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Struck-through foot soldier phrase; Luther worried, thinking about the strategic mind.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the expected first casualty.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the expected reading so the viewer sees the rejection.
storyboard.staging: No soldier drawn; the commander thinking is the casualty.

explainedBy: Setting: Luther stands on the coast of Arboros with an axe, the physical reality the host describes.

storyboard.claim: Luther is on the Arboros coast, swinging an axe.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther on the shore with the axe action named by the callout.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Drops into Arboros.
storyboard.addedInformation: Places Luther in the scene.

storyboard.claim: Luther is hacking at the largest pieces of wood in fury.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Forest set with Luther angry, standing in the wood he is hacking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes what he is doing at the coast.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the action of chopping wood, which no icon depicts.
storyboard.staging: Angry face in the forest: the chopping is the callout, the rage is the face.

storyboard.claim: Luther looks awful after weeks on the road.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Road icon with Luther slumped, exhausted from the journey.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains his physical exhaustion.
storyboard.addedInformation: The road icon reads literally as the long journey.
storyboard.staging: Road icon and slumped exhausted Luther: weeks of travel.

storyboard.claim: His magic is surging in his chest, worse than the exhaustion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther afraid and thinking, the surge felt inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Contrasts the inner surge with the outer exhaustion.
storyboard.addedInformation: Locates the magic in the chest, which a face can show as fear.
storyboard.staging: Afraid face: the surge is inside and felt, not a drawn icon.

storyboard.claim: The magic pushes against his control and issues orders.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther angry, pointing as if receiving a direct command from inside.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Turns the inner surge into the orders he hears.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the magic fights his control, which the rage on his face shows.
storyboard.staging: Angry point: the magic issues orders he is fighting.

storyboard.claim: The magic orders him to free and save her.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Key icon with Luther reaching for it, the means of freeing her.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: The orders named in the previous beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: The key reads as the literal way to free someone held.
storyboard.staging: Reach toward the key: the held object is the subject of the order.

storyboard.claim: The magic growling is not a cute metaphor for missing his mate.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Struck-through metaphor phrase; Luther worried, no romance imagery.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Rejects the romance reading of the growl.
storyboard.addedInformation: Strikes the soft reading so the viewer sees the rejection.
storyboard.staging: No heart icon, since a heart would read romance; the strike carries the rejection.

explainedBy: Cause: the bond's magic acts on the nervous system, and the afraid, slumped body shows the torture.

storyboard.claim: The bond is physiological torture on his nervous system.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, afraid, slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the mechanism.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the effect on the body.

explainedBy: Comparison: godhood acts like a sentient parasite when a bond is threatened, and the callout names the comparison.
noVisual: a parasite is not drawable in the vocabulary; the text names it

storyboard.claim: Godhood works like a sentient parasite in the bond.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, worried, thinking.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the system's comparison.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the magic system's behaviour.

storyboard.claim: Luther strains to stop his magic from leveling half the forest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Forest set with Luther worried and thinking, holding back the eruption.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Describes the cost of his effort.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the eruption would level the forest and kill the allies.
storyboard.staging: Worried effort in the forest: the strain is the claim.

storyboard.claim: The bond is like a highly advanced pacemaker implanted in the chest.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Callout only; a pacemaker has no icon, and a heart would read as love.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the analogy for the magic in his chest.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the bond as a device, not a heart.
storyboard.staging: Callout carries the analogy; no heart icon, which would read as romance.

storyboard.claim: The bond shocks him with thousands of volts when he focuses elsewhere.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther afraid, bracing against the shock of the bond.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Extends the pacemaker analogy into the shock.
storyboard.addedInformation: States the voltage the viewer cannot see.
storyboard.staging: Afraid face: the shock is named by the callout.

explainedBy: Relationship: his magic controls his body like a hostage-taker, and the slumped, afraid figure shows the paralysis.

storyboard.claim: His magic holds his body hostage.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther, afraid, slumped.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains the paralysis.
storyboard.addedInformation: Names the control as hostage-taking.

callout.text: CANNOT STRATEGIZE OUT OF A CRISIS

storyboard.claim: A commander cannot strategize out of a global crisis while bonded.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther worried and thinking in the wide realm, unable to plan.
storyboard.onScreenText: CANNOT STRATEGIZE OUT OF A CRISIS
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Gives the military consequence of the hostage state.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the strategy fails, shown in the thinking face.
storyboard.staging: Worried thinker in the realm: the crisis is too big to plan out.

storyboard.claim: The bond sabotages his role as a military leader.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Game icon for the board, with Luther angry: the missing piece tethered.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Returns to the chess board from the start.
storyboard.addedInformation: Ties the chess board to his military role.
storyboard.staging: Angry face at the board: the bond is the piece sabotaging the game.

storyboard.claim: The compass is a physical manifestation of the psychological hostage situation.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Callout only; the next beat shows the compass.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Transition to the compass.
storyboard.addedInformation: Frames the compass as the physical form of the hostage state.
storyboard.staging: Callout carries the transition; the compass comes next.

storyboard.claim: The golden compass was a gift from the Meos king at Diem's ascension ball.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Compass icon, the golden compass itself.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Introduces the object named in the transition.
storyboard.addedInformation: The compass reads literally as the object named.
storyboard.staging: Compass icon with the callout naming it.

storyboard.claim: Luther holds the compass, which spins in a frantic, aimless motion.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther holding the golden compass, worried by its spin.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Puts the compass in Luther's hand.
storyboard.addedInformation: Shows the compass in his pocket and his worry as it spins.
storyboard.staging: Luther holds the compass worriedly: the spin is the claim.

storyboard.claim: Coril is a magical dead zone that blocks and scrambles magic.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Shore set; the island's dead zone is the callout, not a literal drawing.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Explains why the compass spins.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the island blocks magic, which no icon reads.
storyboard.staging: Shore set with the callout naming the dead zone.

storyboard.claim: The compass should point to Diem but just spins uselessly.
storyboard.concreteVisual: Luther holding the compass, worried, as it spins without a direction.
storyboard.relationToPrevious: Concludes the compass beat.
storyboard.addedInformation: Says the compass fails to find Diem, shown in his worried hold.
storyboard.staging: Worried hold with compass: the useless spin is the claim.
